name: Businesses
alt: Technicians setting up computers in a new office
headline: The basics done properly, so the business can get on with business.
problem: Internet that drops, computers nobody backs up, and no one to call when it stops.
benefits: Staff stop losing hours to IT

name: Schools
alt: Pupils at computers in a Zambian classroom
headline: Computer rooms that survive a term.
problem: Donated computers with no network, teachers on phone hotspots, pupils on the open internet.
benefits: Lessons run without the teacher becoming IT

name: NGOs
headline: Connectivity and data you can report on.
problem: Field offices with donors to report to, sensitive beneficiary data, and grant cycles that do not wait for the internet.
benefits: Support that understands a grant cycle

name: Government
headline: Departmental IT with clear terms.
problem: Ageing networks, printers that do not print, and the public needing e-services access.

name: Mining & Industrial
alt: A site office overlooking red earth and a parked pickup
headline: Reliable technology infrastructure for demanding environments.
problem: Dust, heat, unreliable power, no fibre, and a site that cannot stop.
benefits: Cameras on the gate and the yard

name: Retail
alt: A consultant with a shop owner in a grocery shop
headline: Eyes on the till, and a till that works.
problem: Stock going missing, a point-of-sale that freezes, and mobile money that needs Wi-Fi.
benefits: See the shop from your phone

name: Homes
alt: A Starlink dish mounted above the roof of a house
headline: Internet in every room, and cameras you can check from work.
problem: Wi-Fi that dies in the back bedroom, and no idea who is at the gate.
benefits: The family online at the same time

name: Communities
headline: Skills first, then work.
problem: Young people with phones but no computer skills, and no local route into technology work.
benefits: Courses that show on a profile
